findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update is computed against the org-aware wrapped model, so updates made while the org is disabled can leave stale login entries
findings.body: In update(), the current state of the IDP is loaded via getById(model.getInternalId()), which returns the organization-aware wrapper produced by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. That wrapper's isEnabled() returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled, deleted, or the OrganizationProvider is unavailable. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate then evaluates getLoginPredicate() on this wrapped original: while the org is disabled, test(original) is always false, so the first early-return (!test(original) && !test(updated)) fires for any update that also makes the updated model fail the predicate — e.g. an admin sets hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true, or disables the raw IDP on a broker belonging to a disabled org. However, the .idp.login.* caches are populated from idpDelegate.getForLogin(), which only filters raw attributes (enabled, hideOnLogin, linkOnly, org-public) and does not consider org enabled state, so the raw-eligible IDP's id is still in the cached set and the needed invalidation is skipped. When the organization is later re-enabled nothing invalidates the login cache, getById resolves the stale id as enabled, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean — which only re-checks isEnabled() on the ORG_ONLY/ALL paths — will render a broker the admin explicitly hid from the login page. The 'original' used for the login predicate should be the unwrapped model (e.g. idpDelegate.getById(...)) so the predicate reflects raw stored attributes.

findings.title: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup for literal alias "alias", so the ~21 created identity providers are never removed
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the cleanup registered inside the provider-creation loops uses the literal string "alias": getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) (the same statement is repeated at line 425 for idp-alias-20). No provider with alias "alias" exists, so each cleanup call targets a non-existent resource (404) and, more importantly, the idp-alias-0 … idp-alias-20 providers created by the test are never cleaned up. That leaves over twenty stray brokers — eleven of them enabled, login-visible realm-level providers — in the test realm, which can skew any later test in the class or suite that lists or counts login identity providers. Capture the actual alias in an effectively-final variable and register cleanup with testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove (note the same copy-pasted mistake already exists in testCacheIDPByOrg at line 303 and is worth fixing too).
